content.text:
The files are valid and the paths are correct — the problem is the **preview panel renders the HTML in a sandboxed iframe that can't read sibling files from disk**, so relative `screenshots/...` paths break. (They'd also break if the `.html` is ever moved or shared without the folder.)

The robust fix that works in the preview, in `file://`, and when shared standalone: **embed the PNGs directly into the HTML as base64 data URIs.** I'll do that programmatically so it doesn't bloat the edit:

input.command:
cd "D:/GFA_Cohort_5/CAPSTONE/PRAXIS_SECOND_GITHUB/praxis/docs/presentation" && python - <<'PY'
import base64, re, pathlib
html_path = pathlib.Path("PRAXIS_Demo_Presentation_Template.html")
html = html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

def inline(m):
    rel = m.group(1)
    p = pathlib.Path(rel)
    if not p.exists():
        print("MISSING", rel); return m.group(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(p.read_bytes()).decode("ascii")
    print("inlined", rel, len(b64), "b64 chars")
    return f'src="data:image/png;base64,{b64}"'

new = re.sub(r'src="(screenshots/[^"]+\.png)"', inline, html)
html_path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
print("written, size:", len(new))
PY
